lead.headline: Ship strike kills 1 in Hormuz as Houthis fire on Saudi base
lead.dek: Qeshm's governor blames a 'terrorist enemy' a day before Gulf ministers meet Iran in Oman on the strait
body: An Iranian cargo ship was struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz early Sunday, killing one crew member, Iranian authorities said, hours after Yemen's Houthis announced a missile and drone attack on a base in southern Saudi Arabia.

Qeshm's governor, Amir Teymouri, said the projectile had not been identified and blamed a "terrorist enemy," Euronews reported. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations monitor said a vessel in the strait was hit by an unknown projectile about 5 a.m. local time, caught fire and was being evacuated. Outlets differed on how many crew were wounded, and Iran did not say who fired.

Saudi civil defense said a Houthi projectile wounded two people and damaged a mosque in Jazan's al-Tuwal governorate on Saturday, Al Jazeera reported; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group hit weapons depots at the Sharurah base in Najran but did not say when. Iran hosts Gulf foreign ministers in Oman on Monday on Hormuz shipping. Bahrain said it will not attend.

briefs.headline: Judge rules DHS broke the law in halving FEMA's workforce
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Susan Illston said late Friday that DHS unlawfully usurped FEMA's control of its own staff, cutting it to about half; remedies come in a separate ruling next month.

briefs.headline: DOJ deports Afghan woman in first use of terrorist court
briefs.summary: Records unsealed Friday show Nazira Haji Zada, 47, a lawful permanent resident never charged with a crime, agreed to removal in the first Alien Terrorist Removal Court case since Congress created it in 1996.

briefs.headline: Lucas Fire grows to 4,008 acres as red flag warning holds
briefs.summary: The fire near the Mendocino-Lake county line was 15% contained Saturday night, Cal Fire said, with evacuation orders in nine zones and Highway 20 closed in three places.

briefs.headline: Trump calls Irish unity 'fantastic' on Dublin visit
briefs.summary: Trump met President Catherine Connolly and Taoiseach Micheal Martin on Saturday before heading to his Doonbeg course; Martin's office said Ireland's Northern Ireland policy is unchanged.

briefs.headline: Russian drone hits Kyiv-Warsaw train near Polish border
briefs.summary: A drone struck the locomotive 2 km from Poland with no passengers hurt, Ukrainian Railways said; overnight attacks with 453 drones killed six and injured 43 nationwide.

briefs.headline: Indonesian ferry sinks in the Java Sea with 243 aboard
briefs.summary: The Virgo Transport 8 went down in bad weather early Sunday en route from Surabaya to Banjarmasin; rescuers said one died and more than 100 were missing as 2.5-meter waves hampered the search.

briefs.headline: Fire at Chile nursing home kills 16 residents
briefs.summary: The blaze broke out late Friday at an unregulated home in Pitrufquen, 640 km south of Santiago; 10 of 26 residents survived. President Jose Antonio Kast ordered nationwide inspections.

briefs.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 7,000 cases
briefs.summary: Congolese authorities reported 7,022 cases and 3,398 deaths from the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine, since May; seven provinces are affected, mostly Ituri.

briefs.headline: WVU board approves $156M stadium tower, extends Benson
briefs.summary: The Board of Governors approved construction plans Friday for a $156 million west tower at Milan Puskar Stadium, with demolition to begin in December, and extended President Michael Benson's contract through June 2032.

briefs.headline: No-party ballots jump 74% in WV's first closed primary
briefs.summary: More than 21,000 voters took a no-party ballot in May's closed Republican primary, up 74% from 2022, and fewer Republicans voted than in 2022, Secretary of State data released Wednesday shows.

briefs.headline: Storms close Wood County roads and bring flood warnings
briefs.summary: Wood County dispatch closed Route 50 at I-77 and three other roads Saturday afternoon after flooding, and the National Weather Service warned of life-threatening flooding in eastern Kanawha and Clay counties overnight.

briefs.headline: Senate Health chair will push death penalty bill again
briefs.summary: Sen. Brian Helton, R-Fayette, said Thursday he will reintroduce a bill making the death penalty an option for felony sexual battery of a child under 12; West Virginia abolished capital punishment in 1965.

regional.item: Cabell County commissioners approved $16,000 in hotel-motel tax money Thursday for the West Virginia Pumpkin Festival, set for Oct. 1-4.
A basement house fire in Hurricane on Friday night drew 19 firefighters from three departments; one was treated for an electrical shock.
Gauley season opened Friday with the first scheduled release from Summersville Dam, starting five weeks of releases that draw more than 60,000 visitors.

away.item: The North Bennington Village Block Party runs noon to 2 today on the Park-McCullough grounds, with the volunteer fire department grilling for donations.

hotspots.item: Wide Spot BBQ is back in Webster County after about four years away, The Webster Echo reported Sept. 8, its smoker set up in downtown Webster Springs on Sept. 2.
The Army Corps released a draft environmental study of shore protection at New River Inlet on North Topsail Beach's north end, posted Tuesday; a hearing is Sept. 22.

briefs.headline: Prince George fills CN Centre to remember Mavrik Turnbull
briefs.summary: Between 100 and 200 people attended Saturday's celebration of life for the 3-year-old hockey fan, who died July 6 of neuroblastoma; his family's new foundation will outfit one young cancer patient a year.

briefs.headline: Ex-MLA Coralee Oakes enters three-way race for Quesnel mayor
briefs.summary: Incumbent Ron Paull faces Oakes, Cariboo North MLA from 2013 to 2024, and Brian Waters in the Oct. 17 vote after nominations closed Friday; 18 candidates are running for six council seats.

briefs.headline: BC Housing kept a homeless database to itself since 2016
briefs.summary: CHEK reported Friday the agency has run the federal HIFIS tracking system for a decade but limited access to providers it funds; Victoria council learned of it Sept. 3, after the data went online in August.

briefs.headline: Qualicum Beach clinic set to clear its family doctor wait list
briefs.summary: Four physicians have signed on for the Primrose Medical Centre, opening Nov. 2 with room for 15; volunteers raised $1.5M and the town is adding $400,000 for equipment, the mayor said Saturday.

briefs.headline: Heavyweight George Chuvalo dies on his 89th birthday
briefs.summary: Chuvalo, who went 15 rounds with Muhammad Ali in 1966 and was never knocked down in 93 pro fights, died Saturday, Toronto's Sully's Boxing Gym said. He had dementia and lived in long-term care.

briefs.headline: Trump says Canada 'wants to make a deal very badly'
briefs.summary: Speaking in Dublin on Saturday, Trump said he is not withdrawing from USMCA and tied a deal to Canada dropping tariffs on U.S. farm goods; Canada's counter-tariffs on U.S. products took effect Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Trial backs MRI checks over preventive brain radiation
briefs.summary: A 304-patient trial found MRI surveillance alone cut the risk of cognitive failure or death 40% versus adding cranial radiation in small-cell lung cancer, researchers presented Sunday in Seoul.

briefs.headline: Armored fish evolved 2 ways to crush prey 385M years ago
briefs.summary: Flinders University modeling of eight placoderm jaws from a Western Australia reef found small species crushed prey whole while large ones pierced shells, the team reported in Scientific Reports.

briefs.headline: Buried landscape shows the Andes rose slowly, UCL finds
briefs.summary: A 21.9-million-year-old volcanic blanket up to 1 km thick preserved terrain that puts uplift near 2.5 cm a century, researchers said Friday in Science Advances.

briefs.headline: Penn researchers identify a new inherited eye disease
briefs.summary: A rare EFEMP1 variant found in three unrelated families causes night blindness and peripheral vision loss while the retina looks normal, the team said Friday in JAMA Ophthalmology.

briefs.headline: Amodei calls for slowing AI capability gains
briefs.summary: The Anthropic CEO said Saturday the company will give outside evaluators employee-like access and urged rivals to match it; OpenAI's Sam Altman said it will. The essay is a company statement.

briefs.headline: New Mexico high court holds ChatGPT-using lawyer in contempt
briefs.summary: The court fined Stephen Aarons $5,000 on Wednesday and barred him pending discipline after a brief quoted testimony from witnesses who never existed; he told the court he assumed the summary was accurate.

briefs.headline: Researchers tie May RubyGems package flood to OpenAI agents
briefs.summary: A report by three researchers said hundreds of AI-written packages ran code on a documentation server; OpenAI said its agents did benign tasks and RubyGems said it could not confirm the source.

weather_ear: Sunday's forecast comes from Jim Claudtore at 7:15.
kicker: Summers County and the Mid-Ohio Valley ran no regional line; Sweden counts votes after 2 p.m. ET, and the Topsail Beach hens vote has no posted result a fifth morning.

art.caption: Commercial ships anchored in haze in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, two small motorboats crossing the foreground.
